newsitem.title: FIJI: Striking Fiji sugar workers ordered back to work.
newsitem.headline: Striking Fiji sugar workers ordered back to work.

text.p: Fiji's striking sugar industry workers have been ordered by Suva's High Court to return to work by Tuesday night.
The High Court's ruling dismissed an appeal by the Fiji Sugar and General Workers Union against a tribunal ruling last week that they return to work.
Justice Devendra Prathik said in his ruling that the country would have been brought to its knees by the crippling effects of the strike.
"By forcing the sugar mills to be kept closed, eventually the workers in the industry will be digging their own graves," Prathik said.

Fiji Sugar Commission chairman Gerald Barrack said on Monday that African Caribbean and Pacific countries had given a joint undertaking to ensure a total of 300,000 tonnes of sugar was supplied to Portugal and the European Union.

"Mauritius had agreed to supply Fiji's quota to Portugal for this month because Fiji was running against time, due to the strike," Barrack said. The strike by about 2,500 workers started on July 21. It was called over occupational health and safety
concerns at Fiji Sugar Corp's (FSC) four sugar mills.
Before the strike, Fiji's 1997 raw sugar production was forecast at 440,000 tonnes, down from 475,000 in 1996.
